First, every schedule \((r_n)\in\mathcal R^d\) satisfies \(r_n/a_{b,n}^2\to\infty\) and \(r_n/(na_{e,n}^2a_{b,n}^2)\to\infty\); the second relation is part of \(\texttt{def:admissible-schedules}\), and the first is its algebraic consequence. Second, they are not necessary for the existence of a first-order cross-fitted score inversion with the \((nr_n)^{-1/2}\) honest-diameter rate. \[nr_n\longrightarrow\infty,\qquad nr_na_{e,n}^2\longrightarrow0.\]
Define
\[\begin{array}{c|cc}d&U_d^\star(O)&J_d^\star(O)\\ \hline\mathrm{PN}&AY&(1-A)Y\\\mathrm{PS}&(1-A)(1-Y)&A(1-Y)\end{array}\]
and put \(\pi_{\mathrm{PN}}=e\), \(\pi_{\mathrm{PS}}=1-e\), \(\widehat\pi_{\mathrm{PN},-k}=\widehat e_{-k}\), and \(\widehat\pi_{\mathrm{PS},-k}=1-\widehat e_{-k}\). Let
\[\bar\phi_{t,-k}^d(O)=(1-t)U_d^\star(O)-\frac{\widehat\pi_{d,-k}(X)}{1-\widehat\pi_{d,-k}(X)}J_d^\star(O),\]
\[\bar g_{d,n}(t)=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\bar\phi_{t,-k(i)}^d(O_{i,n}),\qquad \bar\sigma_{d,n}^2(t)=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\{\bar\phi_{t,-k(i)}^d(O_{i,n})-\bar g_{d,n}(t)\}^2.\]
Define \(\bar{\mathcal A}_{n,\alpha}^d=\{t\in[0,1]:n\bar g_{d,n}(t)^2\le z_{1-\alpha/2}^2\bar\sigma_{d,n}^2(t)\}\), and report \(\bar{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}^d=\bar{\mathcal A}_{n,\alpha}^d\) when this set is nonempty and \(\bar{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}^d=\{0\}\) otherwise. Suppose \(\mathcal S_{G,n}^{\partial,d}(r_n;c_G)\ne\varnothing\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). Uniformly over this propensity-only boundary shell,
\[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P_n\in\mathcal S_{G,n}^{\partial,d}(r_n;c_G)}P_n^{\otimes n}\{\Theta_d(P_n)\in\bar{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}^d\}\ge1-\alpha\]
and
\[\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal S_{G,n}^{\partial,d}(r_n;c_G)}E_{P_n^{\otimes n}}[\operatorname{diam}(\bar{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}^d)]=O((nr_n)^{-1/2}).\]
Writing \(b=b(d)\), choose
\[\max\{1-2s_e,\ 2s_b,\ 2s_e+2s_b-1\}<\gamma<1,\qquad r_n=\bar d\wedge n^{-\gamma}.\]
Then
\[nr_n\to\infty,\qquad nr_na_{e,n}^2\to0,\qquad \frac{r_n}{a_{b,n}^2}\to0,\qquad \frac{r_n}{na_{e,n}^2a_{b,n}^2}\to0.\]
For LF-compatible primitives and \(0<c_G\le3/16\), \(\texttt{lem:boundary-shell-nonempty-witness}\) makes every shell in this display nonempty. Thus an alternative propensity-only first-order inversion remains honest and shrinking on explicit schedules outside the sufficient fixed two-nuisance spline regime. This is an internal robustness construction: it refutes no claim in the literature and asserts no negative literature novelty.","depends_on":["ass:iid-row","ass:consistency","ass:conditional-exchangeability","ass:monotonicity","ass:overlap","ass:design-density","ass:holder-propensity","ass:rarity-cap","def:functionals","def:scores","def:learners","lem:identification","lem:generic","lem:uniform-propensity-spline-learning-tails","lem:bounded-iid-normal-approximation","lem:boundary-shell-nonempty-witness"],"proof_tex":"Fix a direction \(d\) and suppress the row index whenever no ambiguity can result. Introduce the transformed variables \(D=A\) and \(R=Y\) for PN, and \(D=1-A\) and \(R=1-Y\) for PS. Put
\[U=DR,\qquad J=(1-D)R,\qquad \pi(X)=P_n(D=1\mid X),\]
so that \(U=U_d^\star\), \(J=J_d^\star\), and \(\pi=e_n\) for PN whereas \(\pi=1-e_n\) for PS. Define
\[\mu(X)=E_{P_n}[R\mid D=0,X],\qquad \nu(X)=E_{P_n}[R\mid D=1,X].\tag{1}\]
Thus \((\mu,\nu)=(m_{0,n},m_{1,n})\) for PN and \((\mu,\nu)=(1-m_{1,n},1-m_{0,n})\) for PS. By \(\texttt{lem:generic}\) and monotonicity, \(0\le\mu\le\nu\le1\) almost surely. Overlap gives \(\varepsilon\le\pi\le1-\varepsilon\). Since the shell fixes \(E_{P_n}[U]=q_d(P_n)=r_n\), iterated expectation yields
\[E_{P_n}[\mu(X)]\le E_{P_n}[\nu(X)]\le \frac{r_n}{\varepsilon},\qquad E_{P_n}[J]=E_{P_n}[(1-\pi(X))\mu(X)]\le\frac{r_n}{\varepsilon}.\tag{2}\]
Write \(t_n=\Theta_d(P_n)\). The identifying functional, whose causal interpretation is supplied by \(\texttt{lem:identification}\), has the unified representation
\[1-t_n=\frac{E_{P_n}[\pi(X)\mu(X)]}{r_n}.\tag{3}\]
The oracle counterpart of the fitted boundary score is
\[T_t(O)=(1-t)U-\frac{\pi(X)}{1-\pi(X)}J.\tag{4}\]
Equations \((2)\)--\((3)\) imply \(E_{P_n}[T_{t_n}]=0\). This distinguishes the causal target from the estimating score used below.

We first transfer the shell information condition to \(T_{t_n}\). In the transformed notation the true orthogonal score from \(\texttt{def:scores}\) is
\[S_{t_n}=T_{t_n}-H,\qquad H=\frac{D-\pi(X)}{1-\pi(X)}\mu(X).\tag{5}\]
Both \(T_{t_n}\) and \(H\) are centered. The two summands in \((4)\) occur on disjoint treatment arms, so, with \(W_n=E_{P_n}[T_{t_n}^2]\),
\[\begin{aligned}W_n&=(1-t_n)^2r_n+E_{P_n}\!\left[\frac{\pi(X)^2}{1-\pi(X)}\mu(X)\right]\\&\le(1+\varepsilon^{-1})r_n.\end{aligned}\tag{6}\]
Furthermore, using \(0\le\mu\le1\) and \(\pi\ge\varepsilon\),
\[E_{P_n}[H^2]=E_{P_n}\!\left[\frac{\pi(X)}{1-\pi(X)}\mu(X)^2\right]\le\varepsilon^{-1}E_{P_n}\!\left[\frac{\pi(X)^2}{1-\pi(X)}\mu(X)\right]\le\varepsilon^{-1}W_n.\tag{7}\]
The boundary shell assumption and \((5)\)--\((7)\) therefore give
\[c_Gr_n\le V_d(P_n)=E_{P_n}[S_{t_n}^2]\le2W_n+2E_{P_n}[H^2]\le2(1+\varepsilon^{-1})W_n.\tag{8}\]
Combining \((6)\) and \((8)\),
\[\frac{c_G}{2(1+\varepsilon^{-1})}r_n\le W_n\le(1+\varepsilon^{-1})r_n.\tag{9}\]
All constants in this display are independent of the law in the shell.

Let \(\widehat\pi_{-k}\) denote the direction-specific fitted propensity, and write \(\widehat T_{t,-k}=\bar\phi_{t,-k}^d\). At the true target,
\[\Delta_{-k}:=\widehat T_{t_n,-k}-T_{t_n}=-\left\{\frac{\widehat\pi_{-k}}{1-\widehat\pi_{-k}}-\frac{\pi}{1-\pi}\right\}J.\tag{10}\]
The fitted propensity is clipped to \([\varepsilon/2,1-\varepsilon/2]\), and the true propensity lies in \([\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\). The mean-value theorem hence gives
\[\left|\frac{\widehat\pi_{-k}}{1-\widehat\pi_{-k}}-\frac{\pi}{1-\pi}\right|\le\frac{4}{\varepsilon^2}|\widehat\pi_{-k}-\pi|.\tag{11}\]
By \(\texttt{lem:uniform-propensity-spline-learning-tails}\), for every fixed \(M>0\), outside an event of probability at most \(C_Mn^{-M}\), simultaneously over the fixed folds, \(\lVert\widehat\pi_{-k}-\pi\rVert_\infty\le C_Ma_{e,n}\). Conditional on a training complement, validation observations have law \(P_n\) and are independent of the fitted function. Since \(J\) is binary, \((2)\), \((10)\), and \((11)\) imply, uniformly over folds and shell laws,
\[|E_{P_n}[\Delta_{-k}\mid\widehat\pi_{-k}]|\le C_Mr_na_{e,n},\qquad E_{P_n}[\Delta_{-k}^2\mid\widehat\pi_{-k}]\le C_Mr_na_{e,n}^2.\tag{12}\]
Conditional Chebyshev inequality on each balanced validation fold and a union bound over fixed \(K\) yield
\[\bar g_{d,n}(t_n)=\mathbb P_nT_{t_n}+O_P(r_na_{e,n})+O_P\!\left(a_{e,n}\sqrt{\frac{r_n}{n}}\right),\tag{13}\]
uniformly over the boundary shell. After division by \(\sqrt{r_n/n}\), the two remainders in \((13)\) are respectively \(O_P(\sqrt{nr_n}\,a_{e,n})\) and \(O_P(a_{e,n})\). The hypothesis \(nr_na_{e,n}^2\to0\) makes both vanish. Consequently,
\[\bar g_{d,n}(t_n)=\mathbb P_nT_{t_n}+o_P\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{r_n}{n}}\right)\tag{14}\]
uniformly over the shell.

The oracle score \(T_{t_n}\) is bounded by a constant depending only on \(\varepsilon\). In view of \((9)\) and \(nr_n\to\infty\), \(\texttt{lem:bounded-iid-normal-approximation}\) gives
\[\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal S_{G,n}^{\partial,d}(r_n;c_G)}\sup_{x\in\mathbb R}\left|P_n^{\otimes n}\!\left\{\frac{\sqrt n\,\mathbb P_nT_{t_n}}{\sqrt{W_n}}\le x\right\}-\Phi(x)\right|\longrightarrow0.\tag{15}\]
For studentization, \((12)\) and conditional Markov inequality give
\[\mathbb P_n\Delta_{-k(i)}^2=O_P(r_na_{e,n}^2)=o_P(r_n).\tag{16}\]
Because \(T_{t_n}\) is bounded and centered, \(E[T_{t_n}^4]\le C_\varepsilon W_n\). Thus
\[\operatorname{Var}_{P_n^{\otimes n}}(\mathbb P_nT_{t_n}^2)\le \frac{C_\varepsilon W_n}{n},\qquad E_{P_n^{\otimes n}}[(\mathbb P_nT_{t_n})^2]=\frac{W_n}{n}.\]
Together with \((9)\) and \(nr_n\to\infty\), this proves
\[\frac{\mathbb P_nT_{t_n}^2-(\mathbb P_nT_{t_n})^2}{W_n}\longrightarrow_P1\tag{17}\]
uniformly. For arbitrary vectors \(x,y\), the reverse triangle inequality after centering gives \(|\operatorname{sd}_n(x+y)-\operatorname{sd}_n(x)|\le\{\mathbb P_ny^2\}^{1/2}\). Applying this with \(x=T_{t_n}\), \(y=\Delta\), and using \((9)\), \((16)\), and \((17)\), we obtain
\[\frac{\bar\sigma_{d,n}^2(t_n)}{W_n}\longrightarrow_P1\tag{18}\]
uniformly over the shell. Equations \((14)\)--\((18)\) imply the uniform studentized limit
\[\frac{\sqrt n\,\bar g_{d,n}(t_n)}{\bar\sigma_{d,n}(t_n)}\rightsquigarrow N(0,1).\tag{19}\]
It follows that the true target belongs to \(\bar{\mathcal A}_{n,\alpha}^d\) with probability tending uniformly to \(1-\alpha\). Whenever this event occurs, the preliminary set is nonempty and the reported set equals it. Hence the singleton fallback cannot remove an accepted true target, and the claimed uniform coverage follows.

It remains to control diameter. The fitted score is affine in its index, with exact slope
\[\bar g_{d,n}(s)-\bar g_{d,n}(t)=-(s-t)\mathbb P_nU.\tag{20}\]
Since \(U\) is Bernoulli with mean \(r_n\), the elementary exponential inequality \(E[e^{-\lambda U}]=1-r_n+r_ne^{-\lambda}\), optimized at the usual multiplicative-Chernoff value, gives
\[P_n^{\otimes n}\{\mathbb P_nU<r_n/2\}\le e^{-nr_n/8}.\tag{21}\]
For fixed fitted weights, the function \(t\mapsto\widehat T_{t,-k}^2\) is convex, so its maximum on \([0,1]\) occurs at an endpoint. Clipping and \((2)\) give, conditionally on every training complement and for either endpoint,
\[E_{P_n}[\widehat T_{t,-k}^2\mid\widehat\pi_{-k}]\le C_\varepsilon\{E_{P_n}[U]+E_{P_n}[J]\}\le C_\varepsilon r_n,\qquad |\widehat T_{t,-k}|\le C_\varepsilon.\tag{22}\]
For completeness, applying \(e^u-1-u\le u^2/[2(1-|u|/3)]\) conditionally to the centered, bounded squared scores on each balanced validation fold shows that, for sufficiently large fixed \(C\),
\[P_n^{\otimes n}\!\left\{\sup_{t\in[0,1]}\mathbb P_n\widehat T_{t,-k(i)}^2>Cr_n\right\}\le Ce^{-cnr_n}.\tag{23}\]
Here convexity reduces the supremum to two endpoints and the union bound ranges over only \(2K\) events, so \(C,c>0\) are uniform over shell laws. On the events complementary to those in \((21)\) and \((23)\), any \(s,t\in\bar{\mathcal A}_{n,\alpha}^d\) satisfy
\[|s-t|\frac{r_n}{2}\le|\bar g_{d,n}(s)|+|\bar g_{d,n}(t)|\le2z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\frac{Cr_n}{n}},\tag{24}\]
because \(\bar\sigma_{d,n}^2(t)\le\mathbb P_n\widehat T_{t,-k(i)}^2\). Hence \(\operatorname{diam}(\bar{\mathcal A}_{n,\alpha}^d)\le C(nr_n)^{-1/2}\) there. The reported diameter is zero when the preliminary set is empty and is always at most one. Taking expectations in \((21)\)--\((24)\), and using \(e^{-cx}\le C_cx^{-1/2}\) for \(x>0\), proves
\[\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal S_{G,n}^{\partial,d}(r_n;c_G)}E_{P_n^{\otimes n}}[\operatorname{diam}(\bar{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}^d)]=O((nr_n)^{-1/2}).\tag{25}\]

Finally, verify the displayed schedules. Since \(s_e,s_b\in(0,1/2)\), each of \(1-2s_e\), \(2s_b\), and \(2s_e+2s_b-1\) is strictly smaller than one. Thus the specified open interval for \(\gamma\) is nonempty. For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(r_n=n^{-\gamma}\), whence
\[nr_n=n^{1-\gamma}\to\infty,\tag{26}\]
\[nr_na_{e,n}^2=n^{1-\gamma-2s_e}(\log n)^{2s_e}\to0,\tag{27}\]
\[\frac{r_n}{a_{b,n}^2}=n^{2s_b-\gamma}(\log n)^{-2s_b}\to0,\tag{28}\]
and
\[\frac{r_n}{na_{e,n}^2a_{b,n}^2}=n^{2s_e+2s_b-1-\gamma}(\log n)^{-2s_e-2s_b}\to0.\tag{29}\]
The strict inequalities defining \(\gamma\) justify each limit. Under LF compatibility and \(0<c_G\le3/16\), \(\texttt{lem:boundary-shell-nonempty-witness}\), for example at \(t=1/2\), supplies a member of every displayed raw boundary shell. The result is therefore an internal comparison of the sufficient regimes of two explicit scores and makes no negative assertion about external work.","status":"proved","justification":"A propensity-only first-order inversion remains honest and shrinking on an explicit ultra-rare schedule class without outcome-regression smoothness.","gap":"This is an internal estimator-robustness construction and does not assert that a published condition is necessary or false.","consumer":"It provides a separate score option when the factual event is rare enough that \(nr_na_{e,n}^2\to0\) and the boundary shell can be verified."}

\[\mu(X)=E_{P_n}[R\mid D=0,X],\qquad \nu(X)=E_{P_n}[R\mid D=1,X].\tag{1}\]
Thus \((\mu,\nu)=(m_{0,n},m_{1,n})\) for PN and \((\mu,\nu)=(1-m_{1,n},1-m_{0,n})\) for PS. By \(\texttt{lem:generic}\) and monotonicity, \(0\le\mu\le\nu\le1\) almost surely. \[E_{P_n}[\mu(X)]\le E_{P_n}[\nu(X)]\le \frac{r_n}{\varepsilon},\qquad E_{P_n}[J]=E_{P_n}[(1-\pi(X))\mu(X)]\le\frac{r_n}{\varepsilon}.\tag{2}\]

\[1-t_n=\frac{E_{P_n}[\pi(X)\mu(X)]}{r_n}.\tag{3}\]
The oracle counterpart of the fitted boundary score is
\[T_t(O)=(1-t)U-\frac{\pi(X)}{1-\pi(X)}J.\tag{4}\]
Equations \((2)\)--\((3)\) imply \(E_{P_n}[T_{t_n}]=0\). This distinguishes the causal target from the estimating score used below.

We first transfer the shell information condition to \(T_{t_n}\). In the transformed notation the true orthogonal score from \(\texttt{def:scores}\) is
\[S_{t_n}=T_{t_n}-H,\qquad H=\frac{D-\pi(X)}{1-\pi(X)}\mu(X).\tag{5}\]
Both \(T_{t_n}\) and \(H\) are centered. The two summands in \((4)\) occur on disjoint treatment arms, so, with \(W_n=E_{P_n}[T_{t_n}^2]\),
\[\begin{aligned}W_n&=(1-t_n)^2r_n+E_{P_n}\!\left[\frac{\pi(X)^2}{1-\pi(X)}\mu(X)\right]\\&\le(1+\varepsilon^{-1})r_n.\end{aligned}\tag{6}\]
Furthermore, using \(0\le\mu\le1\) and \(\pi\ge\varepsilon\),
\[E_{P_n}[H^2]=E_{P_n}\!\left[\frac{\pi(X)}{1-\pi(X)}\mu(X)^2\right]\le\varepsilon^{-1}E_{P_n}\!\left[\frac{\pi(X)^2}{1-\pi(X)}\mu(X)\right]\le\varepsilon^{-1}W_n.\tag{7}\]
The boundary shell assumption and \((5)\)--\((7)\) therefore give
\[c_Gr_n\le V_d(P_n)=E_{P_n}[S_{t_n}^2]\le2W_n+2E_{P_n}[H^2]\le2(1+\varepsilon^{-1})W_n.\tag{8}\]
Combining \((6)\) and \((8)\),
\[\frac{c_G}{2(1+\varepsilon^{-1})}r_n\le W_n\le(1+\varepsilon^{-1})r_n.\tag{9}\]
All constants in this display are independent of the law in the shell.

Let \(\widehat\pi_{-k}\) denote the direction-specific fitted propensity, and write \(\widehat T_{t,-k}=\bar\phi_{t,-k}^d\). At the true target,
\[\Delta_{-k}:=\widehat T_{t_n,-k}-T_{t_n}=-\left\{\frac{\widehat\pi_{-k}}{1-\widehat\pi_{-k}}-\frac{\pi}{1-\pi}\right\}J.\tag{10}\]
The fitted propensity is clipped to \([\varepsilon/2,1-\varepsilon/2]\), and the true propensity lies in \([\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\). The mean-value theorem hence gives
\[\left|\frac{\widehat\pi_{-k}}{1-\widehat\pi_{-k}}-\frac{\pi}{1-\pi}\right|\le\frac{4}{\varepsilon^2}|\widehat\pi_{-k}-\pi|.\tag{11}\]
By \(\texttt{lem:uniform-propensity-spline-learning-tails}\), for every fixed \(M>0\), outside an event of probability at most \(C_Mn^{-M}\), simultaneously over the fixed folds, \(\lVert\widehat\pi_{-k}-\pi\rVert_\infty\le C_Ma_{e,n}\). Conditional on a training complement, validation observations have law \(P_n\) and are independent of the fitted function. Since \(J\) is binary, \((2)\), \((10)\), and \((11)\) imply, uniformly over folds and shell laws,

Conditional Chebyshev inequality on each balanced validation fold and a union bound over fixed \(K\) yield
\[\bar g_{d,n}(t_n)=\mathbb P_nT_{t_n}+O_P(r_na_{e,n})+O_P\!\left(a_{e,n}\sqrt{\frac{r_n}{n}}\right),\tag{13}\]
uniformly over the boundary shell. After division by \(\sqrt{r_n/n}\), the two remainders in \((13)\) are respectively \(O_P(\sqrt{nr_n}\,a_{e,n})\) and \(O_P(a_{e,n})\). The hypothesis \(nr_na_{e,n}^2\to0\) makes both vanish. Consequently,
\[\bar g_{d,n}(t_n)=\mathbb P_nT_{t_n}+o_P\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{r_n}{n}}\right)\tag{14}\]
uniformly over the shell.

The oracle score \(T_{t_n}\) is bounded by a constant depending only on \(\varepsilon\). In view of \((9)\) and \(nr_n\to\infty\), \(\texttt{lem:bounded-iid-normal-approximation}\) gives
\[\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal S_{G,n}^{\partial,d}(r_n;c_G)}\sup_{x\in\mathbb R}\left|P_n^{\otimes n}\!\left\{\frac{\sqrt n\,\mathbb P_nT_{t_n}}{\sqrt{W_n}}\le x\right\}-\Phi(x)\right|\longrightarrow0.\tag{15}\]
For studentization, \((12)\) and conditional Markov inequality give
\[\mathbb P_n\Delta_{-k(i)}^2=O_P(r_na_{e,n}^2)=o_P(r_n).\tag{16}\]
Because \(T_{t_n}\) is bounded and centered, \(E[T_{t_n}^4]\le C_\varepsilon W_n\). Thus
\[\operatorname{Var}_{P_n^{\otimes n}}(\mathbb P_nT_{t_n}^2)\le \frac{C_\varepsilon W_n}{n},\qquad E_{P_n^{\otimes n}}[(\mathbb P_nT_{t_n})^2]=\frac{W_n}{n}.\]

\[\frac{\mathbb P_nT_{t_n}^2-(\mathbb P_nT_{t_n})^2}{W_n}\longrightarrow_P1\tag{17}\]
uniformly. For arbitrary vectors \(x,y\), the reverse triangle inequality after centering gives \(|\operatorname{sd}_n(x+y)-\operatorname{sd}_n(x)|\le\{\mathbb P_ny^2\}^{1/2}\). Applying this with \(x=T_{t_n}\), \(y=\Delta\), and using \((9)\), \((16)\), and \((17)\), we obtain
\[\frac{\bar\sigma_{d,n}^2(t_n)}{W_n}\longrightarrow_P1\tag{18}\]
uniformly over the shell. Equations \((14)\)--\((18)\) imply the uniform studentized limit
\[\frac{\sqrt n\,\bar g_{d,n}(t_n)}{\bar\sigma_{d,n}(t_n)}\rightsquigarrow N(0,1).\tag{19}\]

\[|s-t|\frac{r_n}{2}\le|\bar g_{d,n}(s)|+|\bar g_{d,n}(t)|\le2z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\frac{Cr_n}{n}},\tag{24}\]

\[\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal S_{G,n}^{\partial,d}(r_n;c_G)}E_{P_n^{\otimes n}}[\operatorname{diam}(\bar{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}^d)]=O((nr_n)^{-1/2}).\tag{25}\]

{"id":"lem:cot-vanishing-variance-studentization-comparator","kind":"lemma","statement":"The active in-repository template \(\texttt{stat\_cot\_observational\_efficiency/lem:vanishing-variance-studentization}\) has the following generic bounded-score content. If an i.i.d. triangular-array estimator or score mean has expansion \(n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nU_{i,n}+R_n\), where \(EU_{i,n}=0\), \(|U_{i,n}|\le B\), \(E[U_{i,n}^2]=\sigma_n^2>0\), \(R_n=o_P(\sigma_n/\sqrt n)\), \(\widehat\sigma_n^2-\sigma_n^2=o_P(\sigma_n^2)\), and \(\sqrt n\sigma_n\to\infty\), all uniformly over the law collection, then its studentized statistic converges uniformly to \(N(0,1)\) and the associated two-sided Wald acceptance event has asymptotic probability \(1-\alpha\).","depends_on":["ass:iid-row","lem:bounded-iid-normal-approximation"],"proof_tex":"Let \(\mathcal Q_n\) denote the row-\(n\) collection of laws, and write \(\bar U_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^nU_{i,n}\). All stochastic orders in this proof are uniform over \(Q\in\mathcal Q_n\). Since \(\sqrt n\,\sigma_n\to\infty\), we have \(n\sigma_n^2\to\infty\). Hence \texttt{lem:bounded-iid-normal-approximation} gives
\[
\sup_{Q\in\mathcal Q_n}\sup_{x\in\mathbb R}\left|Q\left\{\frac{\sqrt n\,\bar U_n}{\sigma_n}\le x\right\}-\Phi(x)\right|\longrightarrow0. \tag{1}
\]
Put \(A_n=\sqrt n\,\bar U_n/\sigma_n\), \(B_n=\sqrt n\,R_n/\sigma_n\), and \(C_n=\widehat\sigma_n/\sigma_n\). The remainder hypothesis gives \(B_n=o_Q(1)\). Moreover, because \(C_n\ge0\),
\[
|C_n-1|=\frac{|C_n^2-1|}{C_n+1}\le |C_n^2-1|=\frac{|\widehat\sigma_n^2-\sigma_n^2|}{\sigma_n^2}=o_Q(1). \tag{2}
\]
In particular, \(Q(C_n=0)\to0\) uniformly. On \(C_n>0\), the studentized statistic is
\[
T_n=\frac{\sqrt n(\bar U_n+R_n)}{\widehat\sigma_n}=\frac{A_n+B_n}{C_n}. \tag{3}
\]
For completeness, the uniform Slutsky step follows by an elementary truncation. If \(f\) is bounded and Lipschitz, then on \(\{|A_n|\le M,|B_n|\le\delta,|C_n-1|\le\delta\}\), with \(0<\delta<1/2\),
\[
|f(T_n)-f(A_n)|\le\operatorname{Lip}(f)\left\{2\delta+2M\delta\right\}. \tag{4}
\]
Equation \(1\) makes \(A_n\) uniformly tight, while the complement involving \(B_n\) and \(C_n\) has uniformly vanishing probability by \(2\) and the remainder condition. First let \(n\to\infty\), then \(\delta\downarrow0\), and finally \(M\uparrow\infty\). Thus \(T_n\) converges uniformly weakly to \(N(0,1)\). Applying the same cutoff-smoothing argument as in \texttt{lem:bounded-iid-normal-approximation} upgrades this conclusion at the continuous Gaussian distribution function to
\[
\sup_{Q\in\mathcal Q_n}\sup_{x\in\mathbb R}|Q(T_n\le x)-\Phi(x)|\longrightarrow0. \tag{5}
\]
Therefore, with \(z=z_{1-\alpha/2}\),
\[
\sup_{Q\in\mathcal Q_n}\left|Q\{|T_n|\le z\}-\{\Phi(z)-\Phi(-z)\}\right|\longrightarrow0.
\]

1. DEFINE THE HOLDER NORM (def:holder).
The notation \(\lVert f\rVert_{\mathcal H^\beta}\) is not defined, so the document does not say whether constants have norm \(|c|\) or seminorm zero. This obscures how restrictive the primitive richness conditions actually are. FIX: Define the Hölder norm explicitly. If the intended convention is the usual full norm, state that a constant map \(c\) has Hölder norm \(|c|\), making the all-constants condition equivalent to the corresponding radius being at least one. If a seminorm is intended, state that constants are automatically included and remove the redundant membership language.

This is load-bearing for how restrictive the primitive richness conditions actually are: under the full Holder norm a constant c has norm |c|, making the outcome condition the real-but-mild radius restriction L_{b(d)} >= 1; under a seminorm-only convention constants have seminorm zero and the conditions are automatic. The theorem is valid either way because membership is explicitly assumed, but the convention MUST be stated so a reader can see which.

The symmetric requirement that the directional outcome ball contain every constant in \([0,1]\) is stronger than the displayed construction needs. For the lemma's full t-range, PN uses only constants in \([0,3/4]\), while PS uses only constants in \([1/4,1]\). State the constant-containment requirement over the range the construction actually uses, not the whole of [0,1]. A hypothesis stronger than its proof needs is a defect even when the theorem is true.

The uncapped case is PROVED. Six prose locations still present it as unresolved and contradict the theorem. Prose renders verbatim, so this ships as a false limitation. Replace each field with EXACTLY the text below.

--- FIELD: tldr ---
Direction-specific honest PN/PS inference has minimax expected-diameter order \((nr_n)^{-1/2}\) on every eventually nonempty Gaussian shell indexed by an admissible schedule in \(\mathcal R^d\), provided the primitive rectangular richness conditions hold and \(0<c_G<(1-\varepsilon)/(4\varepsilon)\). The cross-fitted Gaussian upper result is uncapped and requires neither primitive rectangular richness nor this upper restriction on \(c_G\). The derived uncapped witness covers vanishing, nonvanishing, and oscillating admissible schedules, while bounded effective count separately forces nonshrinking diameter. The universal structural score-variance coefficient is sharply \(C_G=\varepsilon^{-1}\).

--- FIELD: honest_scope ---
The proved matched minimax expected-diameter order \((nr_n)^{-1/2}\) extends throughout \(\mathcal R^d\), including nonvanishing and oscillating schedules, for eventually nonempty directional Gaussian shells under the primitive rectangular richness conditions and \(0<c_G<(1-\varepsilon)/(4\varepsilon)\). The cross-fitted upper theorem itself remains uncapped and holds on every stated nonempty directional shell in \(\mathcal R^d\) for any fixed \(c_G>0\). The primitive-richness converse derives an identical-shell witness without using \(\bar d\); the older least-favorable converse remains a valid weaker result under least-favorable compatibility and an eventual cap. Without primitive rectangular richness, or outside the displayed \(c_G\) range, no all-schedule matching converse is claimed. The bounded-effective-count lower theorem is a separate nonshrinking result, not an all-regime confidence procedure. Climate PN or FAR use requires an externally fixed event and verified PN-shell conditions; stroke PS use requires separate PS-shell verification.

--- FIELD: interpretation ---
The operative information scale is the expected factual-event count \(nr_n\). changed.from: Gleser and Hwang prove that, in several errors-in-variables and inverse-regression models, confidence sets for the parameter of interest cannot simultaneously have positive confidence coefficient and finite expected diameter; their result also covers general confidence sets for scalar and vector parameters.
changed.to: Gleser and Hwang (1987, Theorem 1) prove a fixed-sample impossibility theorem under an unbounded-range condition for the scalar target and a boundary likelihood-coalescence condition: no confidence set can have both a strictly positive confidence coefficient and finite diameter almost surely, and hence none can have finite expected diameter. They verify the conditions for most linear and nonlinear errors-in-variables regression models and for inverse-regression problems. Their scalar obstruction extends to vector confidence sets by projection onto an obstructed component. Because the probabilities of causation considered here satisfy \(\Theta_d(P)\in[0,1]\), the required unbounded-range condition fails; consequently their theorem does not imply the bounded-effective-count non-shrinkage result in this note, which is a bounded-parameter analogue rather than an instance of the Gleser--Hwang theorem.
changed.reason: The frozen summary omits the unbounded-range and boundary likelihood-coalescence hypotheses of Gleser and Hwang's Theorem 1 and can therefore be read as a model-free impossibility claim. The replacement states the theorem's operative hypotheses, preserves its errors-in-variables, inverse-regression, and vector-set scope, and records the load-bearing distinction that \(\Theta_d(P)\) is bounded. This is a faithful narrowing supported by the primary paper, Annals of Statistics 15(4), 1351--1362, DOI 10.1214/aos/1176350597, and by the equivalent statement reproduced as Theorem 2.1 of Hwang and Liu (1992).

directive:
D0 REPAIR DIRECTIVE — discharge the logistic-Hessian gap (D0.5 math referee, 2 findings).
Author these changes yourself and re-prove everything they invalidate IN THIS ROUND.
Make no other mathematical change.

THE DEFECT (the referee is correct; do not argue it away).
`def:learners` fits the propensity by minimizing the ridge-penalized logistic loss over ALL of
R^{J_{e,n}}, and applies the clip \Pi_{[\eps/2,1-\eps/2]} to the OUTPUT PROBABILITY afterwards.
So the clip never constrains the optimization. The empirical Hessian is
    (1/N) \sum_i w_i B_i B_i^\top + 2\lambda_{e,n} I,   w_i = \sigma(B_i^\top\theta)(1-\sigma(B_i^\top\theta)),
and nothing bounds w_i below: on a near-separated training sample \|\theta\| grows, the fitted
logits diverge, and w_i \to 0. `def:learners` explicitly contemplates "separated logistic samples",
which is exactly the failure case. The only unconditional curvature floor is 2\lambda_{e,n}=2n^{-2},
giving an inverse bound of order n^2, NOT the asserted O(J_{e,n}). The asserted step is false as
written in BOTH `lem:propensity-spline-learning-tails` and `lem:uniform-propensity-spline-learning-tails`.

REPAIR 1 — CONSTRAIN THE LOGIT IN `def:learners` (definition-replace).
Replace the propensity minimization with a minimization over the compact convex set
    \Theta_{e,n} = \{\theta \in R^{J_{e,n}} : \|\theta\|_\infty \le B\},
for a FIXED, DECLARED constant B depending only on \eps (from ass:overlap), \beta_e, L_e, p and the
spline degree r_e — never on n and never on the sample. Keep the ridge term and the output clip.

This is a change to OUR ESTIMATOR, which is a design choice. It is NOT an assumption strengthening,
and you must NOT discharge the gap by adding any hypothesis about the data, the fitted logits, or
the Hessian. If you find yourself assuming a weight floor rather than deriving one, stop and say so.

You must then DERIVE, not assert, all four of the following:
 (a) LOSSLESSNESS. ass:overlap gives \eps \le e_n \le 1-\eps, so the true logit
     \ell_n = \log(e_n/(1-e_n)) is bounded in sup-norm by \log((1-\eps)/\eps), and is Holder of the
     same exponent \beta_e as e_n (logit is smooth with bounded derivatives on [\eps,1-\eps], so the
     composition preserves the Holder class up to a constant). Show its tensor-product B-spline
     quasi-interpolant \theta^*_n obeys \|\theta^*_n\|_\infty \le \log((1-\eps)/\eps) + C, UNIFORMLY
     IN n -- for the nonnegative partition-of-unity basis the coefficients are controlled by local
     sup-norms of the approximated function. Then FIX B strictly larger than that bound, so
     \theta^*_n is feasible with margin for all large n and the usual approximation rate survives.
 (b) WEIGHT FLOOR. On \Theta_{e,n}, |B_{e,n}(x)^\top\theta| \le \|\theta\|_\infty \le B, because the
     basis is a nonnegative partition of unity (so B^\top\theta is a convex combination of the
     coordinates of \theta). Hence w \ge \sigma(B)(1-\sigma(B)) =: w_{\min}(B) > 0, a constant.
 (c) THE O(J) BOUND. Combine (b) with the partition-of-unity Gram-matrix eigenvalue bound
     \lambda_{\min} \gtrsim J_{e,n}^{-1} (using ass:design-density) to recover the asserted
     O(J_{e,n}) inverse bound. State explicitly where the design-density lower bound enters.
 (d) EXISTENCE, UNIQUENESS, MEASURABILITY, AND THE BOUNDARY. The objective is strictly convex and
     \Theta_{e,n} is compact convex, so the minimizer exists and is unique; replace the
     gradient-descent measurability argument with PROJECTED gradient descent (the projection onto an
     \ell_\infty ball is coordinatewise clipping, hence continuous). Do NOT silently keep using the
     first-order condition \nabla = 0: a constrained minimizer may sit on the boundary. Either prove
     the minimizer is INTERIOR with high probability (\theta^*_n is interior with margin by (a)) and
     confine the normal-equation argument to that event, or carry the variational inequality through.
     Whichever you choose, say which, and handle the complementary event explicitly in the tail bound.

REPAIR 2 — COLLAPSE THE DUPLICATE LEMMA.
`lem:propensity-spline-learning-tails` and `lem:uniform-propensity-spline-learning-tails` assert the
same conclusion and differ only in citing `def:propensity-learner` versus `def:learners`. Keep ONE
(prefer the `def:learners` form, and keep the "no smoothness condition on either outcome regression
is required" clause if it is true of the surviving proof). Delete the other via statement-delete and
rewire every consumer's depends_on to the survivor. Two proofs of one fact drift apart; this is the
same duplication that produced the other defects in this note.

SCOPE. Do not touch any other statement, definition, or assumption. Do not add assumptions. Do not
weaken any headline claim. If after honest work the O(J_{e,n}) bound still does not follow, do NOT
paper over it -- report the obstruction and the best rate you can actually prove.

{"id":"def:learners","name":"fixed-fold ridge-regularized clipped spline learners","construction":"Fix a deterministic balanced fold map \(k(i)\in\{1,\ldots,K\}\). For \(j\in\{e,0,1\}\), set \(s_j=\beta_j/(2\beta_j+p)\) and, for every integer \(n\ge1\), define
\[K_{j,n}=\begin{cases}1,&n<3,\\ \left\lceil(n/\log n)^{1/(2\beta_j+p)}\right\rceil,&n\ge3,\end{cases}\qquad J_{j,n}=(K_{j,n}+r_j+1)^p,\qquad \lambda_{j,n}=n^{-2},\qquad a_{j,n}=\left\{\frac{\log(n\vee3)}{n\vee3}\right\}^{s_j}>0,\]
with \(r_j\ge\lceil\beta_j\rceil\). Let \(B_{j,n}(x)\in\mathbb R^{J_{j,n}}\) be the nonnegative partition-of-unity tensor-product B-spline basis of degree \(r_j\) on the deterministic quasi-uniform grid with \(K_{j,n}\) cells per coordinate. On the training complement \(I_{-k,n}\), with \(N_{-k,n}=|I_{-k,n}|\), use the deterministic fallback \(\widehat\theta_{e,-k,n}=\widehat\theta_{0,-k,n}=\widehat\theta_{1,-k,n}=0\) when \(N_{-k,n}=0\), and skip the next two minimizations. When \(N_{-k,n}>0\), define \(\widehat\theta_{e,-k,n}\) as the unique minimizer over \(\mathbb R^{J_{e,n}}\) of
\[\frac1{N_{-k,n}}\sum_{i\in I_{-k,n}}\left[\log\{1+\exp(B_{e,n}(X_{i,n})^\top\theta)\}-A_{i,n}B_{e,n}(X_{i,n})^\top\theta\right]+\lambda_{e,n}\lVert\theta\rVert_2^2.\]
For \(a\in\{0,1\}\), define \(\widehat\theta_{a,-k,n}\) as the unique minimizer over \(\mathbb R^{J_{a,n}}\) of
\[\frac1{N_{-k,n}}\sum_{i\in I_{-k,n}}\mathbf 1\{A_{i,n}=a\}\{Y_{i,n}-B_{a,n}(X_{i,n})^\top\theta\}^2+\lambda_{a,n}\lVert\theta\rVert_2^2.\]
Set
\[\widehat e_{-k,n}(x)=\Pi_{[\varepsilon/2,1-\varepsilon/2]}\!\left(\frac{\exp\{B_{e,n}(x)^\top\widehat\theta_{e,-k,n}\}}{1+\exp\{B_{e,n}(x)^\top\widehat\theta_{e,-k,n}\}}\right),\qquad \widehat m_{a,-k,n}(x)=\Pi_{[0,1]}\{B_{a,n}(x)^\top\widehat\theta_{a,-k,n}\}.\]
The positive ridge makes every objective coercive and strictly convex, so every learner exists uniquely for every training sample, including separated logistic samples and samples containing no observation from one treatment arm. Each unique minimizer is measurable: deterministic gradient descent from zero with step smaller than the reciprocal of the common gradient-Lipschitz bound converges pointwise to it. Cross-fitting evaluates at observation \(i\) the learner trained on \(I_{-k(i),n}\). Casewise evaluation of the clipped score gives \(|\psi_t^d(O;\widehat\eta)|\le B_\varepsilon=2/\varepsilon-1\) and \(|\psi_t^d(O;\widehat\eta)-E\psi_t^d(O;\widehat\eta)|\le2B_\varepsilon\) for both directions and every \(t\in[0,1]\).","inputs":["\(Z_n\)","\(K\)","\(\beta_e\)","\(\beta_0\)","\(\beta_1\)","\(r_e\)","\(r_0\)","\(r_1\)","\(\varepsilon\)"]}

D0 REPAIR DIRECTIVE — two scoped repairs from the D0.5 panel. Author both yourself and re-prove
anything they invalidate IN THIS ROUND. Make no other mathematical change.

1. ARITHMETIC CORRECTION in `thm:bounded-count-diameter-obstruction` (math referee).
The reproduced chi-square step is misbounded. With \(r_n\le1/2\) and \(t_1\le3/4\), the quantity
\(1/2-p_{1,n}\) is only guaranteed to be \(\ge1/8\), NOT \(\ge1/4\). Consequently the term currently
written \(4\Delta^2r_n^2\) must read \(8\Delta^2r_n^2\).

Propagate the corrected constant through the remainder of that computation and CHECK, do not assume,
that the stated final bound \(\le 8\Delta^2 r_n\) still follows; the referee states it does. If after
honest recomputation any downstream constant or the final bound actually changes, report the true
value -- do NOT preserve the displayed bound by adjusting something else to match. Confirm explicitly
in the proof text which inequality supplies the \(1/8\).

This is a correction toward a WEAKER intermediate constant. Do not "repair" it by tightening a
hypothesis, restricting \(r_n\) or \(t_1\), or strengthening any assumption.

2. THEOREM-LEVEL POSITIONING for `thm:gaussian-frontier` (decision referee).
The headline frontier is not directly compared with the closest already-bibliographed work. Add a
theorem-level distinction against BOTH:
  - Zhang--Wang--Miao causal-attribution inference, and
  - Cuellar--Kennedy regular PC inference,
covering all FOUR axes the referee named: (i) identification regime, (ii) rare-event triangular-array
scale, (iii) estimator, (iv) the honest expected-diameter lower-bound object.

DO THIS AS PROSE ON THE EXISTING NODE -- related-work / justification text on `thm:gaussian-frontier`,
plus bibliography entries if genuinely missing. Do NOT mint new `cited` comparator lemma nodes for
this. Earlier rounds answered positioning findings by adding comparator leaves; the note now carries
seven cited comparators, FOUR of which have zero inbound edges and carry no load. Adding more inflates
the graph without addressing the finding, and each new node then needs its own positioning.

State only what you can attest from the cited sources. If you cannot attest a distinction on one of
the four axes, say so plainly rather than asserting it.

SCOPE. Touch only these two nodes (and bibliography/prose). Add no assumptions. Weaken no headline.
